b7c37f5aca95: Ask: «When you leave your car at a garage, does it matter to you which of the mechanics actually repairs it?» Lead them to the idea that at a garage the person is usually not important — the action is.
caac3d593c2c: In this workshop you pay on collection.
81f74e11eb10: The oil and the air filter have been changed.
8b63c02e3cfa: This is the map of the lesson: four constructions, each one gets its own slides later. Point out that English has close equivalents: you have to, you can hear, they pay, it has been changed.
11a3b5e506a2: «Należy» appears on signs, in rules and in service letters; in conversation «trzeba» is more common. Ask the learner to make one sentence about their own car with «warto» and one with «nie da się».
0ed1c9f79f67: Key point: «było» and «będzie» are always neuter singular, because there is no subject. Example from a car service: «Wczoraj trzeba było czekać na części».
20d8c7d039cb: This is exactly how the list of work is written on an invoice and in a service report. English analogy: replaced, checked, ordered.
e2b52ae60a01: The -no/-to form has no present or future tense and no agent. For the future the garage uses a personal form: «Wymienimy klocki jutro».
27b46eabacbe: How do you open the bonnet in this car?
e5db92fcfd70: Tires are usually changed in autumn and spring.
a6feec730d64: Smoking is not allowed on the workshop premises.
c53fcbb8b770: Note «maskę» and «opony»: accusative, not nominative. It is not “the bonnet opens by itself” but “someone opens the bonnet”.
a8b3a1da9716: The rule is the same as on slide 6: the form comes from the participle. If the participle ends in -ty, the form ends in -to: zdjęto koło, umyto auto.
015cf79fffb8: The most common mistake at the garage is saying «zmiana oleju» (a calque of the English oil change). Ask the student how they have been saying it so far and drill «wymiana oleju».
e06aeeeeabb6: I need to change the tires
